items.short: Notifications during disasters
items.text: Besides the broadcasts of the disaster prevention administrative radio, you can receive information in three ways. (1) Oizumi Town Safety and Security Mail (大泉町安全・安心メール): free of charge; you can also receive it through "Safety and Security" (安全・安心) on the town's official LINE. (2) Emergency alert mail (Area Mail): received automatically, with no registration needed. (3) Telephone notification service: an automated voice message to a landline phone; submit an application form to the Safety and Security Division (安全安心課). How to register is explained on the page "Please use the Safety and Security Mail" (安全・安心メールをご利用ください) (for mail and LINE) and on the page "Telephone notification service for disaster information" (災害情報などの電話配信サービス) (for telephone).

items.short: Transportation in the town
items.text: There are two services. One is the wide-area public bus "Aozora" (あおぞら) (Chiyoda Town – Oizumi Town – Ota City; the timetable is on the town's website). The other is the demand transport service "Hohoemi" (ほほえみ) for the elderly and others. It is for people aged 65 or older, pregnant women, and preschool children. You must register as a user in advance, and call the reservation center from 1 week before the day of use until 1 hour before your desired time. The center is open Monday to Friday, 7:00–17:00. The reservation center's phone number was not on the page we checked. For inquiries, contact the Elderly Care Division (高齢介護課) at 0276-63-3111.

items.short: Childcare contact points and subsidies
items.text:
[Consultation desk]
On April 1, Reiwa 8 (2026), the "Oizumi Town Children and Family Center" (大泉町こども家庭センター) opened.
You can get consultation from pregnancy through the child-rearing period.
For details, contact the Health and Consultation Section (保健・相談係), Children's Future Division (こども未来課) (extension 520).
The Children's Future Division counter is at Window 106 on the 1st floor of the Oizumi Town Hall (大泉町役場) (51-1 Hinode).
The phone number is 0276-63-3111 (main number).
The town's materials did not give a separate address or phone number for the Center alone.

[Main allowances]
The child allowance (from age 0 until the first March 31 after the child turns 18) is paid monthly as follows.
For ages 0 to under 3: 15,000 yen.
From age 3, for the first and second child: 10,000 yen.
For the third child and after: 30,000 yen.
In addition, there are the Child Rearing Allowance, the Orphan Allowance, and the Special Child Rearing Allowance.

[Subsidy for children's medical expenses]
The town subsidizes the out-of-pocket portion when a child receives insured medical care at a medical institution.
It covers children up to high school age.
We could not confirm the detailed conditions of the subsidy.

items.short: How up to date the flood assumptions are
items.text:
The flood assumptions were not produced by the town itself.
The data published by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (for the Tone River and Watarase River) and Gunma Prefecture (for the Kyuhaku River), which manage those rivers, is included by the town in the flood hazard map of the "General Disaster Prevention Map" (総合防災マップ) (pages 29 to 40).
The flood inundation assumed areas for the Tone River and others were designated and published by the Kanto Regional Development Bureau of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism on July 20, Heisei 29.
The town's map was revised as the fiscal year 2023 edition, and corrections to the inundation assumed areas are reflected in it. The page was last updated on March 31, 2025.
In the scope checked this time, we did not find any record that the national government has published a newer assumption for the Tone River.
We have not confirmed when the prefecture published its assumption for the Kyuhaku River.
We could not find tsunami assumptions in the town's materials.
We have also not been able to read the numbers for flood depth this time.

利根川などの洪水浸水想定区域は、国土交通省関東地方整備局が平成29年7月20日に指定・公表したものです。
町のマップは2023年度版に改訂され、浸水想定区域の修正が反映されています。ページの更新日は2025年3月31日です。
今回調べた範囲では、国がこれより新しい利根川の想定を出した記載は見つかりませんでした。県の休伯川の公表時期は確認できていません。
津波の想定は、町の資料からは見つかりませんでした。
浸水の深さの数字も、今回は読み取れていません。
items.back: 洪水の想定は、町が自ら作成したものではありません。河川を管理する国土交通省（利根川・渡良瀬川）と群馬県（休泊川）が公表したデータを、町が「総合防災マップ」の洪水ハザードマップ（29〜40ページ）に掲載しています。利根川などの洪水浸水想定区域は、国土交通省関東地方整備局が平成29年7月20日に指定・公表したものです。町のマップは2023年度版に改訂され、浸水想定区域の修正が反映されています。ページの更新日は2025年3月31日です。今回確認した範囲では、国が利根川についてこれより新しい想定を出した記載は見つかりませんでした。県の休泊川の公表時期は確認できていません。津波の想定は町の資料からは見つかりませんでした。浸水の深さの数字も今回は読み取れていません。

items.short: Notifications for births and deaths
items.text:
Information on birth notifications and death notifications is on the town's "Family Register Notifications (戸籍の届出)" page.
The deadline for a birth notification is within 14 days from the date of birth. The day of birth is counted.
The deadline for a death notification is within 7 days from the day you learned of the death. If the person died abroad, it is within 3 months.
As procedures to be done together with a birth notification, the same page lists "Welfare Medical Expenses and Child Allowance" and "National Health Insurance (enrollment and the lump-sum childbirth and child-rearing allowance)".
The death notification section does not list the procedures to be done together with it (such as pension and health insurance).
The town's "Okuyami (after a death)" page has information on the funeral expense payment, ending notes, and procedures for the park cemetery.
We could not find a single list that combines the procedures for births and deaths.

items.short: National Health Insurance and National Pension
items.text:
Enrolling in and withdrawing from National Health Insurance is handled at the National Health Insurance and Pension Division (国保年金課), Town Hall 1st floor, Window 102.
The phone number is 0276-63-3111, extensions 541 and 542.
It accepts procedures on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.

You can get copies of your residence certificate, seal registration certificates, and family register certificates.

Tax-related certificates such as income certificates and tax payment certificates are issued.

items.short: Transportation for older people far from a bus stop
items.text:
The town operates the on-demand transport for older people and others, "Hohoemi", for people aged 65 and over.
It is for people aged 65 or over who live in the town and can get on and off by themselves.
It takes you from your home to a pick-up/drop-off point (such as hospitals, commercial facilities, and public facilities). You can travel anywhere in the town, and to the Prefectural Cancer Center and Horie Hospital.
It runs Monday to Friday, from 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. It does not run on national holidays or from 12/29 to 1/3.
The fare is per one-way trip: 100 yen within the town and 300 yen outside the town.
From March 2, Reiwa 8 to February 26, Reiwa 9, the fare is free.
First, register as a user. You can apply at the counter (Elderly Care Division, Health and Welfare General Center), by phone, or online.
After registering, call the reservation center between 1 week and 1 hour before you want to use the service.
The contact is the Elderly Care Division (高齢介護課). The registration page gives phone 0276-62-2121 (Health and Welfare General Center, Window 2). The fare subsidy page gives 0276-63-3111 (Town Hall 1st floor, Window 104).

items.short: Information for Foreign Residents
items.text:
Oizumi Town (大泉町) has information for people who have come from other countries.
The multilingual town newsletter "GARAPA" is published on the 10th of every month and is handed out at schools, supermarkets, and other places.
Translated materials such as the "Kurashi no Guide" (くらしのガイド, Living Guide) and the "Gomi Calendar" (ごみカレンダー, Garbage Calendar) are available at the service counter.
On the website of the Multicultural Coexistence Community Center (多文化共生コミュニティセンター), you can read notices in Portuguese, English, and other languages.
For consultations and information, go to the Multicultural Collaboration Division (多文化協働課), Planning Department (企画部), on the 2nd floor of the Town Office (役場). Telephone: 0276-63-3111.
The Center's telephone number is 0276-62-6066.
We could not confirm a Easy Japanese (やさしい日本語) page this time.

To register, send a blank email to bousai.gunma-oizumi-town@raiden2.ktaiwork.jp.

For non-urgent consultations, call #9110 or 027-224-8080 (Gunma Prefectural Police Headquarters, 群馬県警察本部).
Calls are accepted 24 hours a day. At night and on weekends and holidays, the officer on duty responds.

items.short: Town Plans
items.text:
The new town hall (新庁舎) opened for use on May 7, Reiwa 8 (2026).
In the Kamikoizumi (上小泉) district, the town is developing a new industrial park, and work such as installing a retention basin (調整池) in the surrounding area is also underway.
Through its Location Normalization Plan (立地適正化計画), the town aims to build a compact town that can be sustained over the long term.
For the urban planning roads (都市計画道路), the town is acquiring land and taking other steps so that they can be opened to traffic sooner.

上小泉地区では新産業団地の造成を進めていて、周辺の調整池の設置工事なども行っています。
立地適正化計画で、コンパクトで続けやすいまちづくりを目指しています。
都市計画道路は、早く開通させるため用地取得などを進めています。

items.short: Town News
items.text:
The new town hall (新庁舎) was built to open for use in May, Reiwa 8 (2026), and the town has started its operations there.
Contracts for the demolition of the old town hall (旧庁舎) and for the renovation of the Izumi General Park Town Baseball Stadium (いずみ総合公園町民野球場) were submitted as bills to the Town Assembly (町議会) in September, Reiwa 8 (2026).
From fiscal year Reiwa 8 (2026), the tax rates and other aspects of the National Health Insurance tax (国民健康保険税) have changed.
As a measure against rising prices, a payment of 5,000 yen per resident is planned.

items.short: Health checkups, cancer screenings, and vaccinations
items.text:
Information on health checkups and cancer screenings is gathered on the town's official website under "Health and Welfare > Health and Medical Care > Health Checkups and Screenings" (健康・福祉＞健康・医療＞健診・検診). Information on adult vaccinations is under "Vaccinations" (予防接種) in the same category.
The contact office is the Health Promotion Division (健康づくり課), Welfare and Children Department (福祉こども部), Town Hall 1st floor, Room 105, phone 0276-63-3111. For specific health checkups (特定健診), contact the National Health Insurance and Pension Division (国保年金課), Town Hall 1st floor, Room 102.
Advance registration is required for cancer screenings. You can register at the counter, by phone, or through the town's official LINE account.
Out-of-pocket costs (group screening) are: stomach cancer 500 yen, colorectal cancer 500 yen, breast cancer 1,000 yen, and cervical cancer 500 yen. There is an exemption system.
Specific health checkups are for National Health Insurance members aged 40 to 74, and can be received either as a group checkup or an individual checkup (based on the Reiwa 7 fiscal year guide).
For seniors, the influenza vaccine costs 1,000 yen and the pneumococcal vaccine costs 2,000 yen. For the routine shingles vaccination, the live vaccine costs 2,000 yen, and the inactivated vaccine costs 5,000 yen per dose.
For vaccinations, make a reservation by phone with a contracted medical institution.

items.short: For people living with dogs and cats
items.text:
The contact office for dog registration, rabies vaccination, and the subsidy for spay/neuter surgery is the Environmental Maintenance Division (環境整備課), Urban Construction Department (都市建設部), Town Hall 1st floor, Counter 108.
The phone number is 0276-63-3111.
Register your dog within 30 days of getting it. The fee is 3,000 yen.
The rabies vaccination is required once every year. Group vaccinations are held in spring (around May) and autumn (around October), and the fee is 2,950 yen. The fee for the vaccination certificate tag (注射済票) is 550 yen.
The subsidy for spay/neuter surgery is 3,000 yen for males and 5,000 yen for females.
We could not confirm who to contact for lost pets, or how to evacuate with pets during a disaster. Please ask the Environmental Maintenance Division (環境整備課).

items.short: Applying for Nursery Schools and After-School Care (Gakudō)
items.text:
[Nursery Schools and Certified Centers for Early Childhood Education and Care (Category 2 and 3 certification)]
Apply at the Education and Childcare Division (教育保育課), Town Hall 1st floor, Window No. 107.
Applications for admission in April of Reiwa 9 (fiscal year 2027) are accepted from October 9 to November 10, Reiwa 8 (2026) (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays).
Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.
Applications must in principle be submitted in person. If that is difficult, you may also send them by mail (they must arrive within the application period).
For Category 1 certification at kindergartens and certified centers for early childhood education and care, apply directly to the kindergarten or center.
Foreign nationals must submit a copy of their residence card (在留カード).
[After-School Care (Gakudō Hoiku)]
Apply at the children's center (児童館) in the elementary school district your child attends.
For Reiwa 9 (fiscal year 2027), applications are accepted from November 2 to December 15, Reiwa 8 (2026) (9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding 12:00 to 1:00 p.m. and the center's closed days).
For use starting partway through the school year, applications are accepted at any time, and you can also apply online.
North Children's Center (北児童館) 0276-63-3820, West Children's Center (西児童館) 0276-62-4689, South Children's Center (南児童館) 0276-63-1721, East Children's Center (東児童館) 0276-62-0133.
[Phone]
Education and Childcare Division (教育保育課) 0276-63-3111.

The town website has a guide for displaying the site in multiple languages by automatic translation (machine translation).

items.text:

The guides for registering for the Safety and Security Mail (安全・安心メール), the telephone delivery service, and the steps for adding the town as a friend on LINE are also in the same three languages (map pages 3–4).
The town website can be switched to Portuguese, English, Spanish, Nepali, and Chinese by automatic translation. Because this is machine translation, the content may differ slightly.
Pictograms are displayed at evacuation shelters.
A Spanish-language disaster prevention map and a version in Easy Japanese were not found in the materials that were read.
The language of the messages sent by email or LINE could not be confirmed from the materials.

items.short: Lost dogs and cats
items.text:
[If your pet is lost (owners)]
Contact one of the following: the Gunma Prefecture Animal Protection Center, Eastern Branch Office (群馬県動物愛護センター東部出張所), the Gunma Prefectural Police Oizumi Police Station (群馬県警察大泉警察署), or the Oizumi Town Office Environmental Maintenance Division (環境整備課).
Town Office (Environmental Maintenance Division): 0276-63-3111. Reception is open on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.
Animal Protection Center, Eastern Branch Office: 0276-55-0731.
The Oizumi Police Station phone number was not given on the town page we read.

[If you find a lost dog or cat]
For stray dogs and wild dogs, contact the Animal Protection Center, Eastern Branch Office (動物愛護センター東部出張所) at 0276-55-0731.
If the Town Office takes in a dog and an owner has already reported it missing, the Town Office will notify the owner. If no report has been made, the dog is handed over to the Eastern Branch Office and kept there for a set period.

[Information on sheltered dogs and cats]
You can check the prefecture's pages: "犬" protection (shelter) information, "猫等" protection (injured) information, and the information on lost dogs and cats / missing animals.
The town's page "飼い犬・飼い猫の迷子の情報を公開します" also lists lost-pet information for owners who asked to have it posted. Listings stay up for 1 month.

items.short: Vacancies at Nursery Schools and Certified Centers for Early Childhood Education and Care
items.text:

If you want to know about vacancies, please contact the Education and Childcare Division (教育保育課).
The counter for enrollment applications is the Education and Childcare Division (教育保育課), Education Department (教育部), at Counter 107 on the 1st floor of the Oizumi Town Hall (大泉町役場).

For kindergartens and Type 1 certification at certified centers for early childhood education and care, you apply directly to each facility.
For applications during the school year, the deadline is the 10th of the month before the month you want to enroll.

items.short: Emergency Call Device for Older Adults
items.text:
The town lends emergency call devices to older adults who live alone and others who may need one.
When you press the button on the device, it connects you to a reception center that the town contracts to run. If you suddenly become ill and need help, the center will respond according to your situation.
You can also get health advice. Once a month, the center also calls to ask about your physical condition and to check that you are safe.
If you have a landline phone at home, the town will lend you a device that attaches to the landline. It comes as a set with a wireless pendant-type call device.
If you do not have a landline, the town will lend you a portable phone unit that can send emergency calls (it has no telephone function).
The service is for older adults, generally aged 65 or over, who live alone and always need someone to watch over them in daily life because of a chronic illness or similar condition, and for others in a similar situation.
There is no charge.
Before you apply, please talk to the Senior Care Division, Senior Welfare Section (高齢介護課 高齢福祉係). Application forms are available at the counter. You can also download them from the town website.
For inquiries and applications, contact the Senior Care Division, Senior Welfare Section (高齢介護課 高齢福祉係) at 62-2121 (phone). The town newsletter does not give the area code.
You can also apply online: "緊急通報装置貸与" (Emergency Call Device Loan).

items.short: Applying for Long-Term Care Certification
items.text:
To apply for Long-Term Care Certification (要介護認定), submit an application form at the town's counter.
In addition to the person themselves or their family, the Community General Support Center (地域包括支援センター), a home-care support provider (居宅介護支援事業者), or a long-term care insurance facility (介護保険施設) can also apply on their behalf.
The counter is the Elderly Care Division (高齢介護課), Welfare and Children Department (福祉こども部), Counter 104 on the 1st floor of the Town Office Building (庁舎). The phone number is 0276-63-3111. This was read from the "Contact" section of the page.
What to bring:
・People aged 65 or older: the Long-Term Care Insurance Card (介護保険被保険者証).
・People aged 40 to 64: your health insurance eligibility information needs to be confirmed.
・On the application form, write the name, hospital, and address of your primary doctor.
・Applications made on or after April 1, Reiwa 8 (2026) use a new form.
The steps are as follows.
1. Submit your application.
2. Town staff or others visit your home for a home-visit survey. The town also asks your primary doctor for a written opinion.
3. A computer makes a determination, and the Long-Term Care Certification Review Committee (介護認定審査会) reviews it.
4. The result is sent to you. The time from application to notification is set at within 30 days. If notification cannot be made within 30 days, a delay notice will be sent.
5. Once the result is out, a care plan is made and you can use the services.
Information is on the town's official page "Long-Term Care Certification" (要介護認定). The PDFs of the application form and the power of attorney form are also on that page.

items.short: Support for Using the Adult Guardianship System
items.text:
Oizumi Town has the "Adult Guardianship System Use Support Program Subsidy" (成年後見制度利用支援事業補助金) to help people use the adult guardianship system.
It covers costs (revenue stamps, registration stamps, postage stamps, medical certificates, and expert evaluation) when someone other than the town mayor files the petition.
Compensation paid to adult guardians and similar roles is also covered. The upper limit is per month: 28,000 yen for those living at home and 18,000 yen for those living in a facility.
There is also a procedure in which the town mayor files the petition on the person's behalf. In this case, the town pays the filing fee, registration fee, and similar costs in advance. People who are able to bear these costs will be billed later.
For the Daily Life Independence Support Program (日常生活自立支援事業), we found no description of a program to help people use it on the town pages we checked.
